author: Appleman, Roy E.; Burns, James M.; Gugeler, Russell A.; Stevens, John
title: United States Army in World War II — The War in the Pacific: Okinawa: The Last Battle
publisher: Historical Division, Department of the Army, Washington, D.C.
notes: Okinawa from ICEBERG's planning to the end of organised resistance, written by four historians who were with the forces in the Ryukyus — which is why it is the earliest of the Green Books for the Pacific and the closest to its events. It is also unusually full on the Japanese side, with chapters on the Thirty-Second Army's plan of defence; where that rests on captured documents and prisoner interrogation the derivation should be said, because it is a wartime American reading of Japanese intentions. First printed 1948, CMH Pub 5-11-1, LC 49-45742, read off the title page of the 1993 CMH facsimile. Same reachability note as source:morton-1962.
